evidence: app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:12-15 computes totalPages = Math.floor(user_count/limit)+1. With 50 users and limit 50 it returns 2. showingLast (line 18) compares currentPage to totalPages, so on page 1 the Next button stays active. next() (lines 30-38) then sets offset = min(50,50) = 50, and the members endpoint (app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22-26) returns an empty page. Math.ceil(user_count/limit) gives the right page count.

admin-group.js.es6:34 clamps offset to user_count. The showingLast guard (line 31) normally keeps offset+limit below user_count. The empty page only happens because totalPages over-counts on exact multiples (issue 0), and fixing totalPages with Math.ceil removes it. The suggested clamp max(user_count - limit, 0) would also break page alignment: with 120 users and limit 50, the last page would start at 70 instead of 100, so currentPage = floor(offset/limit)+1 would be wrong. The symptom is real, but the root cause is elsewhere and the proposed fix is wrong.

app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:25 sets group.visible = params[:visible] == "true", which gives false when the param is missing. The column defaults to true (db/migrate/20140422195623_add_visibile_to_groups.rb:3; app/models/group.rb:310). However, the admin UI always sends visible: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js asJSON sends visible: !!visible, and new groups are built with Discourse.Group.create({ visible: true }) (admin_groups_route.js:26). Only direct API callers that leave out the param are affected, and the old code (params[:group][:visible] == "true") behaved the same way. Worth hardening, but this PR did not introduce it.

groups_controller.rb:22-32 (create) sets only name and visible. The client sends alias_level in asJSON (discourse/models/group.js, asJSON alias_level: this.get('alias_level')), and the admin form has an alias-level combo box (admin/templates/group.hbs:43). The chosen alias level is silently dropped when a group is created. update (line 37) handles it, but create does not.

groups_controller.rb:38 sets visible = params[:visible] == "true" on every update, so a partial update that omits visible makes the group invisible. The only client, Discourse.Group#save (models/group.js), always sends visible via asJSON, so the UI is not affected. The pre-PR update_put had the same line (payload[:visible] == "true"). The point is fair for API robustness, but it has no impact on current callers.

app/models/group.rb:272-274: Group#add does users.push(user), which inserts the GroupUser row right away for a persisted group. groups_controller.rb:65-82 then calls group.save, which only re-validates the unchanged group (name format and alias_level inclusion) and almost never fails. So the non-atomic scenario is real in theory but unlikely. A more concrete problem the reviewer missed: adding a user who is already a member breaks the unique index index_group_users_on_group_id_and_user_id (group_user.rb schema notes), raising RecordNotUnique and returning a 500.

groups_controller.rb:90 calls group.users.delete(user_id) on has_many :users, through: :group_users (group.rb:8). In Rails 4.1.8 (Gemfile.lock:30), delete on a has_many :through deletes the join rows with delete_all and skips GroupUser callbacks. The counter_cache lives on GroupUser's belongs_to :group, counter_cache: "user_count" (group_user.rb:2), so groups.user_count is not decremented. The existing Group#remove (group.rb:276-278) uses destroy for this reason. spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb:118-130 only checks group.users.count, so the test misses the stale counter.

discourse/models/group.js:21 now returns undefined (`return ;`) instead of Ember.RSVP.resolve([]). But no caller chains on the result: admin_group_route.js:13 and group-members.js.es6:11 call model.findMembers() and ignore the return value; removeMember and addMembers call self.findMembers() inside .then and ignore it; next and previous in admin-group.js.es6 return it from Ember actions, where the return value is not used. The claim that callers sometimes treat it like a promise does not hold. Returning a resolved promise would only be a consistency improvement.

discourse/models/group.js:23 clamps offset with Math.min(user_count, ...), which allows offset == user_count. This repeats issues 0 and 1. In practice offset only reaches user_count through the totalPages over-count (admin-group.js.es6:12-15) combined with next() (line 34). On the first load user_count is 0, so offset is 0, which is fine. Fixing totalPages fixes it. The claim that this "breaks page count math" is overstated: totalPages depends only on user_count and limit.

groups_controller.rb:71-75 (add_members) runs User.find_by_username plus an INSERT through group.add for each comma-separated username, so it is N+1. It could use one User.where(username_lower: usernames.map(&:downcase)) lookup. But this is an admin-only endpoint where an admin types a handful of usernames, so n is small. The pre-PR update_patch had the same per-user loop. The performance impact is negligible.
